Boyos de Pan

Sephardic · Medium · Makes about 16 boyos

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
Boyos — the little rolled pastries of the Sephardic diaspora, from Istanbul to Cairo to Caracas wherever the Ladino kitchens traveled — are the Sabbath morning's own: a soft yeast dough rolled thin, spread with a savory filling (the spinach-and-cheese or the meat's row), rolled to a small spiral, and baked to a golden crescent. The name runs bulemas, boyos, and bizochos by the community's port; the architecture — thin dough, savory filling, the small roll — is the constant of five centuries' wandering.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The dough

  • the dough's medium, the #16 msemen's law

The filling (the classic spinach)

  • the dryness's law)
- **Squeeze the spinach dry — the filling's whole law.** The wilted greens squeezed in a towel to the last drop: a wet filling floods the dough's thin layers and the boyos' bottoms sodden. The dough's medium is oil, the rolled-thin law of the #16 msemen carried — the softer yeast dough here, but the board's oil and the thin roll the same craft. - **The bridge:** the filling rotates by the community and the week — the spinach-and-feta's classic, the ground meat's heartier, the potato's gentle — and every port's kitchen kept its own. The dough's softness is the boyos' own: softer than bread, closer to the msemen's supple cousin.

Boyos de Pan

Prep: 45 minutes, plus 1 hour rising · Cook: 30 minutes · Total: About 2 hours 20 minutes · Makes about 16 boyos

Ingredients

The dough

  • 400 g flour; 1 tbsp sugar (about 10 g); 1 tsp instant yeast (about 4 g); 1 tsp salt
  • 1 egg (about 50 g), beaten; 60 ml olive oil (about 55 g); 180 ml warm water (approximately)
  • Extra oil for the rolling's board — the dough's medium, the #16 msemen's law

The filling (the classic spinach)

  • 500 g spinach, washed and stemmed, wilted 2 minutes and squeezed very dry (about 300 g squeezed — the dryness's law)
  • 200 g feta or a mix of feta and mozzarella (about 200 g), crumbled
  • 3 scallions or ½ an onion (about 75 g), minced; a handful of parsley or dill (about 15 g), chopped
  • ½ tsp black pepper; a grate of nutmeg; 1 egg yolk (about 20 g), to bind
  • The top: 1 egg beaten with a splash of water; sesame or nigella seeds (about 15 g)

Instructions

  1. **Make and rest the dough (1 hour).** Knead the dough's elements 8 minutes to a smooth, soft, slightly tacky ball; rise covered until doubled — 1 hour in a warm kitchen. Checkpoint — the risen dough: puffed, supple, and relaxed — the stretch's own readiness, and the dough must roll thin without springing (the rest's full hour is the guarantee).
  2. **Roll, fill, roll (30 minutes).** With oiled hands on the oiled board, stretch or roll half the dough to a thin 30 cm square — translucent-faint at its center (the #16's law); the spinach filling spread to a thin, even layer over all of it; and the square rolled from one edge to a tight cylinder, cut crosswise to 4 cm pieces — each piece's spiral visible, pressed gently to a squat roll. Repeat with the second half. Checkpoint — each boyo: a visible spiral at its face, the filling's layer coiled within — and the roll set seam-down on the parchment, the filling fully enclosed (an open spiral leaks its cheese to the pan's burning).
  3. **Rise briefly and bake (25 minutes at 190 °C).** The shaped boyos rested 15 minutes under a cloth (the second, brief rise — the softness's insurance), brushed with the egg's wash, scattered with sesame, and baked 22 to 25 minutes to a deep gold — the spiral's ridges darker than the valleys, the cheese's scent rising. Checkpoint — eating test, warm from the oven's cooling: the dough's soft-gold tender bite giving to the spinach-and-feta's savory depth — the herbs' green, the nutmeg's whisper — the spiral's layers in each mouthful, the sesame's toast over. It should taste like the diaspora's own port: the one pastry that every community's kitchen kept, and the Sabbath's morning argument in a hand's size.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Bottoms soggySpinach under-squeezedThe towel's last drop — the filling's law
Spiral unrolled at the bakeCut ends un-pressedThe seam-down set, the gentle press
Dough fought the thin rollUnder-restedThe full hour's rise

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The baked boyos keep 2 days (the reheat a covered 10 minutes at 170 °C); the dough keeps 1 day refrigerated after its rise, the filling 2 days separately — the Sabbath morning's assembly station. - Variations: the meat-filled heartier row, the potato's gentle, the cheese's simple. The #16 msemen is the dough-craft's master; the #38 pastilla is the layered canon's crown — the boyos are the diaspora's own small seat between.
